transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in today because... I've just started to feel, in a quiet but stubborn sort of way, that the best version of my life is already behind me. I've always been someone who figures things out, but lately it just seems like no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling like myself.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been days, weeks, or longer?
It's been much longer than days or weeks. It actually started after a hiking injury I had a little over three years ago. So, I guess it's been right about three years and three months now.
Over these three years, has this low mood been pretty much constant the whole time, or have there been stretches—weeks or months—where you felt back to your normal self before it returned?

I don't think there have been any real stretches where I felt completely back to normal. It's been pretty constant, honestly. I mean, I haven't really noticed any specific weeks or months where it just lifted and I felt like my old self again. It's just sort of... always there in the background.

During these three years, has there ever been a period of at least two weeks where your mood or other symptoms got noticeably worse than your usual baseline—like major changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or interest in things?

No, I wouldn't say there was ever a time where it got noticeably worse like that. It hasn't really dipped down into anything major. It's just... well, it's just been this same, steady feeling the whole time. I haven't noticed any sudden changes in my sleep or appetite or anything like that.

Over these past three years, has this low mood ever been severe enough to seriously interfere with your ability to work, care for yourself, or maintain relationships, or has it generally stayed at a level where you could still manage your day-to-day responsibilities?

I can still manage the day-to-day things, mostly. I get up, I take care of the house, I do what needs to be done. It hasn't stopped me from doing the basics. But... I've definitely stepped back from a lot of other things. I used to do some mentoring, go to community events, get together with people to play music... and I had travel plans. I just don't do those things anymore. So, I guess I'm managing, but my world is just a lot smaller than it used to be.
Besides this low mood, have you noticed changes in your appetite—eating more or less than usual—since this all started three years ago?
No, not really. My appetite has been pretty steady. I still eat my regular meals, so... no, I haven't noticed eating any more or less than I usually do.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep since this started—trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping more than usual?

No, my sleep hasn't really changed. I go to bed around the same time and wake up around the same time I always have. I haven't had any trouble falling asleep, and I'm not sleeping the day away or anything like that. It's just been pretty normal.
Over these past three years, have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or trouble making decisions that you didn't have before?

No, I haven't really noticed any problems with that. My concentration seems fine. I can still read a book or follow a conversation without losing my train of thought. And making decisions... well, I don't feel like I struggle with that any more than I used to. So, no, no real changes there.
Over these past three years, have you noticed feeling more tired or low on energy than you used to, even when you haven't exerted yourself more than usual?

Yes, I have noticed that, actually. I mean, I still get up and do my normal routine—I do the shopping, and I still tinker with my projects. But... well, even small things seem to drain me now. Just setting up for a mentoring session or walking through a community event, it leaves me feeling completely worn out. And it's a kind of tired that a nap doesn't really seem to fix.
Over these past three years, have you noticed feeling more critical of yourself or having lower self-confidence than you used to?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't feel any worse about myself than I did before. I still know what I'm capable of, especially with my mentoring and my projects. I don't really beat myself up or feel like I'm lacking confidence. It's just the energy that's missing, not how I view myself.
Over these past three years, have you found yourself feeling hopeless about the future?

Yes, I have. Actually, that's the main reason I decided to come in and see you. It’s just this... quiet, but stubborn feeling I've developed that the best version of my life is already behind me. I've always been someone who plans things out, but lately, I just feel like no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling like myself again. So, yes, I suppose I do feel a bit hopeless about what's ahead.
